correct_answer: Yes — the curriculum committee motion 23-14 with its accepted amendment constitutes an approved teach-out provision; her continuous enrollment and v4 catalog year entitle her to the original equivalency regardless of the DegreeWorks configuration.
rationale: The critical signal is in the unpublished Canvas course shell — the curriculum committee minutes document Motion 23-14 with an accepted friendly amendment explicitly granting continuous-enrollment students their v4 equivalencies. Curriculum committee motions are binding institutional policy once approved by vote (7-2), regardless of whether the minutes were subsequently submitted to Faculty Senate for informational filing. Faculty Senate receives minutes as a reporting function, not an approval function for curriculum decisions — curriculum authority is delegated to the committee. The student has maintained continuous enrollment since Fall 2022 under the 2022-23 catalog year, satisfying both conditions of the amendment. Answer A applies the wrong policy version — the v5 agreement governs new students but the amendment specifically carved out continuing students. Answer C misunderstands governance structure — the committee's vote IS the decision; Senate filing is administrative, not ratifying. The motion was approved in committee; Karen's sabbatical affected the paperwork trail, not the legal standing of the vote. Answer C overstates catalog year protections — catalog year guarantees degree requirements but does NOT automatically preserve all transfer equivalencies, which are governed by articulation agreements. The correct answer requires the specific teach-out amendment, not a blanket catalog year argument.
